title: Incremental UX probes for tool-call composability (PRD - notes)
summary: Working PRD sketch for a small, measurable experiment: add a lightweight streaming frame and SDK probes to enable speculative client-side rendering + composable tool-call handoff semantics. The goal is to validate whether exposing minimal 'probe' frames and deterministic merge rules reduces perceived latency for tool-integrated flows without increasing backend complexity or safety risk.
context_and_motivation: Problem: many hosted-api integrations experience UI latency when a model decides to call tools mid-stream. Existing approaches either block until tool execution completes or emit heavy structured frames that require complex client logic. That increases SDK surface area and slows developer adoption. This doc proposes a narrow experiment that instruments the streaming protocol and SDKs with explicit, minimal 'UX probe' frames so clients can speculatively render partial results and gracefully reconcile with final tool outputs.
goals: Reduce perceived end-to-end latency for common tool-call flows (search, calendar lookup, code execution) by enabling speculative client updates.
Keep server-side semantics simple: no added transactional guarantees beyond current call/response; probes are hints only.
Test SDK ergonomics: provide a small, discoverable API that integrates with existing streaming callbacks and is easy to adopt in web and mobile clients.
Measure impact on end-user error rates and hallucination surface when speculative content is later replaced by authoritative tool responses.
non_goals: Not attempting to change model routing, not introducing new long-running stateful transactions, and not building full two-phase commit for tools. This experiment avoids adding new security-sensitive tooling endpoints in the first iteration.
requirements:
API and SDK requirements (minimal):
- Streaming frame type: 'probe' (compact JSON line) that carries a stable id, intention label, optional partial payload, and a confidence score.
- Handshake: client can opt-in per-session to receive probes via request header 'X-Redwood-Probe: true'. Default: off.
- Merge rule: any later authoritative tool frame with the same id replaces probe content atomically; SDKs must expose an onProbe and onResolve callback.
- Size cap: probes limited to 2 KB.
- Telemetry: emit metrics for probe_sent, probe_resolved, probe_replaced, probe_timeout.
- Safety: probes must not contain raw executable code or secrets. If a tool returns sensitive data, servers must suppress corresponding probe content.
sdk_ergonomics_proposal: JS SDK: expose StreamingClient.on('probe', fn) and on('probe:resolve', fn). Provide a default UI helper that wraps a DOM element and animates the transition. Python SDK: pass callbacks to stream.iter_lines(probe_callback=...). Mobile: expose platform-native hooks (iOS/Android) with small helper components in the Redwood mobile kit. Emphasize opt-in, small surface area, and a single import in starter templates. Ensure graceful fallback when probes are not supported (no-op).
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (internal): implement probe frames on staging, JS SDK helpers, and a simple reference web demo (search + tool). Collect telemetry.
Phase 1 (alpha): opt-in developer preview for 50 customers via flag. Documentation + migration guide.
Phase 2 (wider beta): expand to more tool types, harden safety filtering.
Phase 3 (GA): enable probes by default for non-sensitive endpoints and add SDK UI components to official packages.
metrics_and_success_criteria: Perceived latency delta (time-to-first-meaningful-paint) reduced by >= 20% for probe-enabled flows compared to baseline.
No >1% increase in user-visible content retractions (probe shown then removed) across alpha users.
Adoption: at least 25% of alpha customers enable probes and integrate SDK callbacks within 8 weeks.
No security incidents attributable to probe content leakage during alpha.
privacy_and_safety: Probes are de-privileged hints. Server-side filtering removes personally identifiable information and any content classified by the safety pipeline as sensitive. Probes must not surface raw credentials, PII fragments, or unredacted documents. Add explicit flags to disable probes for customers with strict data residency or privacy requirements.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: clients may rely on speculative probes and show incorrect facts. Mitigation: confidence score required; default UI patterns must show probes as 'suggested' with visual affordance that content is provisional. Risk: added complexity in SDKs. Mitigation: keep API minimal and provide reference implementations. Risk: increased telemetry volume. Mitigation: sample probes for telemetry (configurable sampling rate).
implementation_notes: Backend: add probe emission points in tool-call orchestration path; ensure probe emission is independent and does not delay tool invocations. Telemetry: add probe lifecycle events to existing event pipeline. SDK: add utilities in hosted-api-js and hosted-api-py, and a small react component in the web-kit. Tests: integration test that ensures probe->tool_result replacement is deterministic and idempotent. Performance targets: probe handling should add <1ms p99 CPU overhead in streaming path.
open_questions: Should probes be allowed from model-only flows (no tool) or strictly tied to tool-call handoffs?
What default UI should we ship in SDK to maximize adoption while avoiding opinionated UX?
How to version probe frame schema without breaking older SDKs? Consider a small version field in the frame.
next_steps: Build a 2-week spike: implement probe frames on staging, 1 reference demo, and a short usability test with 5 internal engineers. Prepare a simple migration doc and gather initial telemetry to decide whether to proceed to alpha.
references: Notes: linked internal playbooks and UX research. See CONFLUENCE-UX-2247 for the original rationale, JIRA-PRODAPI-1128 for backend work, and PR #612 for the initial SDK helpers.
